The Citrus Kasuri Weft Selvedge is a 14oz Japanese selvedge denim distinguished by its complex weft dyeing technique. Beneath the indigo surface lies a vibrant interior created using traditional Kasuri methods.
Rather than inserting solid-colored weft yarns, Kasuri dyeing involves binding and selectively dyeing sections of yarn before weaving. This results in alternating yellow and green segments along the same yarn, producing organic, patterned coloration rather than uniform stripes.
As the denim wears and abrasions develop, the citrus-toned weft gradually reveals itself through the indigo surface. Due to the labor-intensive nature of Kasuri dyeing, this fabric is used sparingly, making it both expressive and rare.

When we started development for the Fall/Winter '25 collection, we had been wear-testing an original 1940s N1 Deck Jacket and looked at how we could do it in our own way. There were a couple things we immediately noticed that we wanted to change.
The alpaca lining was warm…too warm. And itchy as all hell. Practical? Absolutely. But we like our garments to be comfortable, and one of the silly ideas we always consider is: could you wear this comfortably with a t-shirt? Not with alpaca you couldn’t - so we softened it up and opted for a wool/poly pile as the liner. It also helped keep this from being too expensive.
We also wanted to update the fit and give it a little more room everywhere while still maintaining the boxier fit. And in order to make the jacket feel as worn is as our originals, we garment dyed and washed down the jacket so comes with some developed wear right out of the box.
We kept all the OG details we loved; the asymmetrical button flap closure over the zip front, the herringbone tape on the throat latch edges, the hidden elastic cuffs, the reinforced collar details, and even the waist drawstrings.

p-ironheart-10367684542730.d:
The “Big Buck” is a unique collaboration with Simmons Bilt in Scotland, based on our traditional Western shirt silhouette and handmade from European deerskin. The leather used comes from deer living in the hills and mountains of Germany and Austria. As these are wild animals, many hides display natural scars — a byproduct of antlered males fighting during the rutting season. This shirt is the original version of the Big Buck and features a single back panel, which on newer models has been replaced by a three-panel design to allow the use of more unscarred sections of hide.
The tanning method is an old and traditional process known as Sämischgerbung, a chemical-free technique that, while time-consuming, produces an incredibly soft yet hard-wearing leather. We source this leather from Kolesch Tannery (https://www.gerberei-kolesch.de/) — the oldest working tannery in Germany — where it is both tanned and hand-dyed.
